notes.content:
# Harbor launch plan

Ship the mobile app to the public on the 14th of next month. Three gates before then: beta feedback closed, the onboarding rewrite merged, and the pricing page signed off.

- [x] Beta invite list
- [x] Crash reporting
- [ ] Store listing copy
- [ ] Launch email

# Q4 roadmap

Three workstreams: Harbor launch, the sync rewrite and the support backlog. Harbor gets two thirds of the team until launch week, then the sync rewrite takes over.

# Beta feedback, week 2

41 testers active. The top complaint is the sign-up flow (nine fields). Second is that offline mode is hard to find. Nobody mentioned speed, which is the first time.

# Onboarding rewrite

Cut sign-up from nine fields to four. Ask for the name later, on the first share. Draft screens are on the launch board.

# Pricing page

One free tier and one paid. The comparison table moves above the fold; the FAQ answers the refund question in its first line.

# Sprint 14 retro

What helped: measuring before changing anything. What did not: two days lost reading code instead of running it. Keep the Thursday demo.

# Sync rewrite, first notes

The conflict rule is last-writer-wins today, which silently drops edits. Proposal: keep both versions and ask, the way a document merge does.

# Why the list felt slow

It was not the database. Every row re-measured its own height on scroll. Caching the height per row took a long list from 40ms a frame to 6.

# Store listing

Five screenshots, dark and light. The first line has to say what it does in under ten words: notes that sort themselves, offline.

# Launch email draft

Subject: Harbor is out. One paragraph, one screenshot, one button. Send at 9 in each time zone, not all at once.

# Support backlog triage

63 open tickets. 20 are the same export question; one help article closes them. Billing questions go to the new form.

# Hiring a designer

Portfolio review on Tuesday. Looking for someone who has shipped a product end to end, not only screens.

# Launch metrics

Day-one installs matter less than week-two retention. Track: notes created in the first week, and whether people come back on day 8.

# Launch risks

1. The store review takes longer than a week.
2. Sync conflicts surface under real load.
3. The pricing page is not signed off in time.

# Thursday demo notes

Showed the new onboarding to the whole team. Feedback: the progress dots read as a carousel. Replace them with a step count.

# Team offsite ideas

One day, no laptops. A walk in the morning, the roadmap in the afternoon, dinner somewhere with a long table.

# Public API, maybe

Three people in the beta asked for one. Not before launch. Write down the read-only version so the idea is not lost.

# Portugal trip, overview

Ten days in May: four in Lisbon, a day in Sintra, three in Porto, two in the Douro valley. Train between the cities, a car only for the valley.

# Lisbon, where to stay

Alfama for the walk-everywhere feel, but the hills are steep with luggage. Príncipe Real is quieter and close to the metro.

# Sintra day trip

Train from Rossio, 40 minutes. Pena Palace first thing, timed ticket. Quinta da Regaleira in the afternoon when the tour buses leave.

# Porto, three days

Ribeira at sunset, the Livraria Lello early or not at all, and a port lodge tour across the bridge in Gaia.

# Douro valley

Hire a car in Porto. Stay one night at a quinta near Pinhão; the river road from Régua to Pinhão is the drive to do.

# Flights

Out to Lisbon, back from Porto, so no day is lost going back. Booked, seats 14A and 14B.

# Trains

Lisbon to Porto on the Alfa Pendular, 2h50. Tickets open 60 days ahead and are half price if booked early.

# Things to eat

Pastéis de nata at the Belém bakery, bifana from a counter, francesinha in Porto once, grilled sardines anywhere with a queue.

# Packing list

- Walking shoes with grip (the pavements are polished stone)
- A light jacket for the evenings
- Plug adapter
- The rail pass printout

# Trip budget

Roughly 1,900 for two, flights included. The quinta night is the splurge; everything else is mid-range.

# Useful phrases

Obrigado or obrigada, depending on who is speaking. Uma bica is an espresso in Lisbon and um cimbalino in Porto.

# Photo spots

Miradouro da Senhora do Monte at golden hour. The Dom Luís I bridge from the upper deck. Arrive early, leave the tripod.

# Sourdough log

Loaf 6: 78% hydration, 20 hour cold proof. Best crumb yet, still pale underneath. Next time the stone goes one shelf lower.

# Starter feeding

1:5:5 at night, ready by morning in a warm kitchen. In winter it needs the oven with only the light on.

# Weeknight dinners

Five that take under 30 minutes: miso salmon, chickpea curry, lemon orzo, egg fried rice, and the tomato soup below.

# Roast tomato soup

Roast the tomatoes and garlic first, add a little smoked paprika, blend half and leave the rest chunky.

# Chickpea curry

Onion, garlic, ginger, a spoon of curry paste, a tin of chickpeas and a tin of coconut milk. Spinach at the end.

# Pizza night

The sourdough discard makes a good thin base. 48 hour dough, hottest oven, steel on the top shelf.

# Meal prep Sundays

Cook grains and one sauce for the week. Freeze half the soup. Saves about four evenings.

# Trying pastéis de nata at home

Shop-bought puff pastry, rolled tight into a log. The custard needs the hottest oven the kitchen has; mine scorched at 250.

# Knife sharpening

Whetstone at 15 degrees, 1000 then 6000 grit. Every two months, or when the tomato test fails.

# Spice drawer

Toast whole spices before grinding. Buy small, label with the month.

# Half marathon plan

Twelve weeks to the October race. Three runs a week: one easy, one tempo, one long. The long run grows by a kilometre a week.

# Week 4

Easy pace is still too fast. Slow the Tuesday run down until it is boring, then hold it for three weeks.

# Physio, left knee

Foam roll the IT band after every long run. Single-leg squats twice a week, three sets of ten.

# New running shoes

The old pair has 700 km on it. Try two in the shop, run on the treadmill in both.

# Sleep notes

Screens off at 10:30 helps more than anything else tried. Coffee after 2pm costs about forty minutes.

# Fuel on long runs

A gel every 40 minutes past the first hour. Practise it in training, never new on race day.

# Morning mobility

Ten minutes: hips, hamstrings, thoracic rotation. Done before coffee or it does not happen.

# Dentist

Check-up booked for the 21st. Ask about the night guard.

# Race day checklist

- Bib and pins the night before
- Same breakfast as the long runs
- Start slower than feels right

# Thinking in Systems

Stocks and flows, and why a delay inside a feedback loop makes a system oscillate instead of settle. The bathtub example finally made it click.

# Four Thousand Weeks

The point is not to get everything done; it is to choose what to neglect on purpose. Pairs well with the systems book.

# The Design of Everyday Things

A door that needs a sign has failed. Affordances, signifiers and feedback: the three words I now use in every design review.

# Atomic habits, the useful bits

Make the good thing the easy thing. Lay the running kit out the night before; it works better than willpower.

# On writing short

An essay about cutting: every sentence should earn its place, and the first draft is for finding out what you think.

# Podcast: slow productivity

Do fewer things, work at a natural pace, obsess over quality. Fewer open loops means less time spent switching.

# Reading list

- Designing Data-Intensive Applications
- The Mom Test
- A Pattern Language
- Ways of Seeing

# Designing Data-Intensive Applications

Chapter 5 on replication is the one to reread before the sync rewrite. Leaderless replication and read repair.

# The Mom Test

Ask about their life, not your idea. Specifics in the past beat opinions about the future.

# A line worth keeping

From a poem read on the train: attention is the beginning of devotion.

# A Pattern Language

A window place: people are drawn to light. True of rooms, and oddly true of app screens too.

# Garden, spring jobs

Cut back the lavender after the last frost. Move the rosemary into the sun. Sow the beans in the second week of April.

# Boiler service

Due in March. The pressure keeps dropping to 0.8; mention it. The engineer last time said the valve was worn.

# Paint for the study

Two samples on the wall: a warm white and a pale green. The green wins in the afternoon light.

# Home insurance renewal

The renewal quote went up 30%. Compare three before the 1st; the old policy covers accidental damage, keep that.

# Houseplants

The fiddle leaf wants the east window and less water. Repot the monstera in spring.

# Shelves in the hall

Stud finder first. Two brackets per metre, 6mm plugs. The oak board needs a coat of oil before it goes up.

# Bin days

Recycling is every other Tuesday; food waste every week. The calendar is on the fridge.

# Bike service

The gears skip under load. New chain and a cassette check before the summer.

# Wi-fi in the back room

One mesh point on the landing fixed it. Speed in the study went from 4 to 180.

# Offline as the headline

Beta testers did not know Harbor works offline. What if that is the first thing the store page says, not the fifth?

# Notes as a map

A node on a board could be a real note, so the map and the notebook stay one thing.

# A five-line journal

One line each: what happened, what I learned, what I am grateful for, what tomorrow needs, one word for the day.

# A photo book of the trip

Twenty pictures, one per page, with a line from these notes under each.

# The garden as a system

Compost is the stock, kitchen scraps the inflow. The delay is about six months, which is why it never feels like it is working.

# Teach what I just learned

Write a short post after each book: the one idea I would keep. It forces the reading to be active.

# A bread habit

Bake every Saturday for twelve weeks and log each loaf. Same habit rule as running: make the start easy.
# Harbor launch board
# Portugal trip
